claims.claim: Land verifiers/check_substrate_pins.py — a read-only guard enforcing the measured_against substrate pins in verifiers/baseline.json (sha256 for omp and opencode; mtime ns-exact for omp; opencode mtime unpinnable and documented as such) — with a committed self-test fixture set, the family exit-code ladder (0 match / 1 drift-or-pin-absent / 2 environment / 3 baseline), and no execution of the guarded binaries.
claims.before: measured_against pins are inert: grep shows zero reads across all six verifiers; corrupting the omp sha or deleting the whole block still exits 0 (round-22 scouts M6/P1/P8, proven executably). Substrate movement (round 21's omp rebuild) reached the gates only through downstream literal failures.
claims.after: the script exists in verifiers/, its --self-test is green on committed fixtures (assertion count recorded), the live run exits 0 with all pins holding, and six red probes behave as designed: (a) sha drift -> exit 1 naming the pin; (b) mtime-only drift -> exit 1 naming omp_binary_mtime; (c) missing binary -> exit 2; (d) corrupt baseline JSON -> exit 3 without traceback; (e) missing/null measured_against -> exit 1 (vacuity, the M6-D2 defect class); (f) deleted single pin -> exit 1 PIN_ABSENT (the P7 silent-shrink defect class). Capabilities table gains the row; the corpus doc + README row land; corpus-baseline re-records 52->53 for the new corpus file.
claims.counting_command: python3 verifiers/check_substrate_pins.py (exit 0); python3 verifiers/check_substrate_pins.py --self-test (exit 0, assertion count recorded); the six red probes on /tmp copies as above
claims.falsifier: any red probe exiting differently than specified, a traceback on malformed input, any execution of omp/opencode binaries (opencode.log must not gain lines), self-test non-green, or the capabilities row claimed without the demonstrated run
